body:
shadow wrote:
 As for the
> majority, it will be enough to make them aware of the existence of the
> new ideology and remind them of it frequently."

Wouldn't a new political party provide both an organization and platform
for the publicity to bring out such awareness and keep it up?  It would
also provide a legitimate means to collectively finance the effort.  The
reason the Democrats and Republicans are so afraid of a viable third
party is even if it does not have a majority it wouldn't need one. 
Merely by preventing either the Dems or Repubs from having a majority a
third party would either be the swing vote between them deciding issues
or if the Dems and Repubs united many of the radicals in both parties
would split off.  Either way, the stranglehold of the two parties would
be broken for the first time in a hundred years and we might have a
chance for real change.


> note 32 "it is even conceivable (remotely) that the revolution might
> consist only of a massive change of attitudes toward technology
> resulting in a relatively gradual and painless disintegration of the
> industrial system."

Is this the only means or hope TK holds out for peaceful change?  After
all, the original design of Democracy is supposed to allow for
Revolution without violence.  The average person, or majority, will
fight against violent revolution until such time as conditions have
become so bad that they are going hungry and losing loved ones.  Once
things have gone this far unless there is a distinct outside oppressor
nearly all chance of controlling the outcome is lost. Don't get me
wrong, I like the IDEA of anarchy it is just that the resultant rule of
force which inevitably arises is a definite step back.  (Even though all
rule is eventually base on force some systems do manage to insulate
greater numbers of people from its exercise than others, as well as to
use it in a clearly regulated and predictable manner)
	In other words is it not better to make ourselves heard with votes than
with deaths, especially since it is death we are trying to avoid?
